outcomes.witnessed: Automated evidence asserts the previous commit is preserved or a recoverable journal is exposed, and no partial destination is advertised.

currentControls.summary: The core project boundary accepts only exact schema 16, rejects pre-release schemas 1 through 15 with a typed re-import-required error, and opens newer schemas as opaque clones read-only without overwriting them. Schema 12 normalizes a bounded declarative feature-requirements manifest into a deep-frozen clone, rejecting duplicate requirement IDs, noncanonical feature IDs, unsupported dispositions, and invalid fallback source-kind references or digest syntax. Its pure evaluator classifies caller-declared availability without executing project-supplied identifiers or mutating the manifest. Current-schema, current-format .scape paths preserve the manifest and fallback-only source assets, including collision remapping. On current-format exact schema 16 routes, each rendered-fallback claim is bound to its canonical asset descriptor before collision lookup or storage. Export snapshots the admitted project root and complete source records, serializes those same sources and the bounded normalized fallback manifest used for validation, rejects project/source toJSON rewrites, and hashes completed asset output before manifest write or destination commit; import verifies each asset body size and SHA-256 before source or project publication. Inspection performs descriptor binding but does not hash asset bodies. A stable selected-product capability registry treats only strict `true` as available and unregistered IDs as unknown. Current schema 16 create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile the reserved `soundscaper.audio-effects` requirement for maintained first-party effects in track, group, send, or master racks, including disabled effects and inactive racks; publisher-authored audio-effects requirements take precedence, missing and foreign effects do not trigger it, and reserved-ID conflicts reject. The same paths reconcile the reserved `soundscaper.video-effects` requirement for maintained first-party effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips, including disabled effects; publisher-authored video-effects requirements take precedence, missing and foreign effects and stacks on non-video clips do not trigger it, and reserved-ID conflicts reject. The same paths validate schema-16 nested track folders as closed top-level metadata plus authoritative closed per-sequence nodes, require exact derived sequence trackIds and project-wide track and folder preorder, and reconcile nonempty state to the reserved `soundscaper.track-folders` requirement with display name `Nested track folders`, disposition `bypass`, and no fallback. Soundscaper registers `org.soundscaper.capability.track-folders` available with native folder commands and tree UI, while Framescaper registers it known but unavailable, so nonempty state is preserved read-only there; the capability is absent from both rendered-fallback eligibility sets, and publisher-authored audio or video fallback for it rejects before activation. Before playback, audio render, video preview, or video export, a bounded transient projection derives inherited folder mute, solo, and hidden state into leaf track flags. It runs before rendered-fallback projections, privately authenticates its enumerable marker across explicit transient clones, rejects a forged marker before hierarchy traversal, and leaves canonical folder state, leaf-local flags, routing, history, and persistence unchanged; collapsed and height remain UI-only. Exact schema 16 is evaluated from the actual project history before activation, incompatible projects become intrinsically read-only, and an existing same-ID tab's stored read-only declaration wins over the ignored incoming document's flags. The report remains deep-frozen across per-tab session metadata clones and the document snapshot. Current-format .scape inspection receives the same selected-product evaluator as a provider-owned option that caller options cannot override; exact schema 16 is evaluated after archive and source validation but before project collision lookup and returns a deep-frozen report, while future schemas return null and featureRequirements is not traversed. The localized dialog shows bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared disposition, defaults focus to Cancel, and supports Escape dismissal and focus restoration. After activation, the maintained active workspace persistently displays a non-dismissible document-level notice from the active tab's incompatible report. It derives a frozen subset containing only unavailable and unknown items, recomputes counts, and shows bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared dispositions while the owning tab is active. Available items are excluded, evaluator messages and fallback internals are not read, and the notice exposes no activation controls or generic runtime fallback or third-party-loading claim; the separate role-defined audio whole-mix, role-defined whole-project video, and first-party clip-local videoEffects playback controls bind their active indicators to frozen metadata. Compatible and future-schema null reports render no notice. For an exact schema 16 registered `audioEffects` item that is unavailable with declared `bypass` and effective `bypassed`, activation derives a bounded, non-persisted engine projection before activation side effects while the canonical project, history, source loading, and persistence remain unchanged. Only active, enabled, not already bypassed maintained first-party effects in track, group, send, and master racks become minimal bypassed playback copies. The lower-only 4,096-effect ceiling rejects instead of truncating; effect params, context, and state are not read. Deep-frozen per-tab and snapshot metadata drives one affected-object inventory with localized labels and no controls under the first qualifying requirement. Unknown and third-party effects, rendered fallback, offline render and export behavior, and activation controls remain outside this audio slice. For an exact schema 16 registered `videoEffects` item that is unavailable with declared `bypass` and effective `bypassed`, activation derives a bounded, non-persisted preview-playback projection before activation side effects while the canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, save paths, offline render, and video export remain unchanged. The lower-only 4,096-effect ceiling, 256-character stable-ID ceiling, and 128-character effect-type ceiling reject instead of truncating; effect params, context, state, and opaque payloads are not read. A layout-only witness allocates no PCM or output bytes while admitting the exact constructible 69,793,218,560-byte (65 GiB) RF64 boundary and rejecting the next frame. Realtime publication waits for every streamed clip to settle and fails closed with the first stable source-underrun identity before commit; interactive playback retains silence-on-underrun behavior. Its conservative 41,943,384-byte path-owned binary maximum is below the planned 64 MiB buffered-binary budget with zero PCM payload retention; a second run cancels after the first coalesced 4 MiB PCM destination write without close, commit, or partial publication. Maintained Chromium and Firefox WAV, AIFF, BWF, and BW64 coverage comprises ten aggregate format/engine cases through an injected File System Access target and simulated mobile planner profile. The assembler requires exact Soundscaper product/target manifests and a version-matched package inventory before network access. Electron Builder's beforePack hook rejects staged runtime-summary, manifest, or notice drift present when the hook runs; its afterPack hook independently revalidates the copied runtime inventory, manifest, and notice before fuse or signing work. Publication authorizations mirror the fail-closed licensing gates. Offline regressions prove invalid preflight never enters desktop assembly or invokes Wrangler, tested staged drift is rejected at beforePack, and post-copy tampering cannot reach fuse work. The manifest review marker and payload digest detect inconsistent edits but do not authenticate independent human approval.

The production Web build generates separate install metadata for Soundscaper and Framescaper and one content-addressed application-shell inventory. Generation permits only regular nonsymbolic output, at most 4,096 assets, 25 MiB per asset, and 256 MiB aggregate, and binds exact byte lengths and SHA-256 digests with the service-worker template into the release identity. The stable no-store root worker recomputes that identity, sequentially fetches only the allowlist, verifies every complete body before caching it, and writes readiness last. Failed installation removes only the candidate; activation requires readiness and claims clients before retiring older complete shell caches. Production HTTP(S) registration is nonblocking, while Electron, non-HTTP documents, and unsupported browsers are unchanged. The Web preferences expose an explicit FFmpeg runtime download; no runtime download occurs implicitly. Its strict boundary permits only the pinned production origin and content-addressed versioned release layout, bounds pointer bytes to 64 KiB, manifest bytes to 512 KiB, each file to 64 MiB, aggregate files to 65 MiB, and streamed chunks to 4 MiB, and verifies pointer-bound manifest and asset lengths and SHA-256 digests. For non-identity Content-Encoding, decoded stream bounds and digests remain authoritative while cached responses are normalized. CacheStorage transactions isolate candidates and copy complete files before active-state publication; cooperative same-origin Web Locks serialize each fresh-state commit and cleanup, same-release retries reuse a complete cache, and post-commit cleanup is best effort. The store revalidates exact cached body lengths and SHA-256 digests and retains one prior complete release. Only state-committed active and previous descriptors are eligible through the service worker, whose cached responses are streamed through exact byte-length and SHA-256 verification before completion. The editor prefers a ready installed release and otherwise keeps its pinned network fallback. Focused Node and Chromium workflows cover shell identity, failed install and activation retention, two-product offline reload, explicit download, encoded, altered, and partial runtime handling, serialized publication, previous-version recovery, committed-only serving, cached-body revalidation, and orphan denial.

This is consumer-side consistency and rollback, not an independent authenticity root: a compromised asset host can replace the pointer with a new internally self-consistent release.
